gaps.note: Edit during Kevin's initial offer attempt, cutting to Mark.
Edit covering Charles walking to the hallway to make a phone call.
Edit covering Charles returning to the tank.

stage_a.note: Friendly, energetic delivery with consistent smiling and engaged tone throughout the pitch.
Shows clear excitement when explaining the product's size and demonstrating its ease of use.
Very approachable, offers drinks to the panel, smiles and jokes with them.

venture.description: A compact smartphone breathalyzer that plugs into the audio jack to measure blood alcohol content and help users make safer decisions.
venture.note: The ask is clearly stated at the beginning of the pitch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles introduces himself, his company Breathometer, and asks for 250k for 10 percent, setting up a party scenario.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles asks the sharks if they would care for a glass of champagne to demonstrate the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin enthusiastically accepts the offer of champagne from Charles.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori accepts the champagne, noting she thought he was joking.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles hands out the glasses of champagne to the panel.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin tells Charles that Daymond doesn't like champagne and takes his glass.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles hands the extra glass to Kevin, noting it is Daymond's favorite drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles asks the sharks what they should toast to.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin toasts to Charles, joking that sometimes it ends badly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles resumes his pitch, introduces the smartphone breathalyzer, demonstrates how it plugs in, and explains its features.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Charles if the product is already on the market and currently being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles explains they launched on Indiegogo, sold 4000 units in 30 days, and generated 140k in revenue.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark briefly explains to Lori that Indiegogo is a crowdfunding site like Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Charles what the retail price of the breathalyzer is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles directly answers that they sell the units for forty-nine ninety-nine.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks about the liability risk if someone relies on the device, gets drunk, and harms someone.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles states it doesn't replace good judgment, noting they provide manuals and clear disclaimers to mitigate liability.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if she can come up and try the breathalyzer device.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles agrees and invites Lori to come up and test the device.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokes that if Lori can walk in her heels, she already has her answer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles walks Lori through plugging in the device, starting the app, and having her blow into it.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori notes her reading of point zero four means she would be legal to drive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles confirms to Lori that her reading means she is legally allowed to drive.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks if the device can also tell if a person has bad breath.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles confirms they are looking into a halitosis sensor and developing it as a multi-function device, including for diabetes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Charles about his background, specifically if he is a software or hardware developer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles explains he used to code and that he built and sold his last company within eighteen months.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks why Charles didn't invest his own money from his previous success into this new venture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles clarifies he put in the initial 50k and has raised half a million dollars from angel investors.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks Charles what he plans to use the new investment money for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles states the funds will be used strictly for manufacturing the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin mentions that other countries have zero tolerance and asks about the trend.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles agrees, noting the NTSB is trying to push the US limit down from point zero eight.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark expresses that he is a big fan of the sensor business and sees it as the future.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin announces he is going to make Charles an offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark preempts Kevin and offers five hundred thousand dollars for twenty percent of the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles acknowledges Mark's offer but asks for a chance to talk to the other sharks.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Mark if he would let her go in on the deal to handle retail.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark declines Lori's request, stating he is not worried about the retail aspect right now.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori argues that retail is a long-term benefit, disagreeing with Mark's dismissal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin offers two hundred and fifty thousand dollars for fifteen percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles notes that Kevin's offer is much less dilutive than Mark's twenty percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin points out that his offer also provides significantly less cash than Mark's.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles proposes opening the round to involve more than one shark to close a full one million dollar round.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin suggests letting the sharks do the entire one million dollar round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles confirms that is exactly what he is proposing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark states he does not want to work with the other sharks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies with Charles if his goal is to raise a full million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles confirms that he does want to raise a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin points out that Mark's current offer is not giving him enough money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert offers to join Kevin, providing another two hundred and fifty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori joins Kevin and Robert, adding another two hundred and fifty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert clarifies their combined offer is seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars for thirty percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond tells Charles it is smart to surround himself with people smarter than him.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond matches the original ask, offering two hundred and fifty thousand dollars for ten percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond complains about how hard it is to work with the other sharks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles suggests a million dollar straight equity deal to get all five sharks involved.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin states they would need a significant discount to do a deal with all five sharks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin explains that Mark needs the lion's share because competing is expensive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles playfully urges Mark Cuban to join the all-shark deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond revises his stance, saying he will go in if Mark goes in.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks Charles what equity share he would get in this scenario.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles reiterates the goal is to get all five sharks involved.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark tells Charles it is now his turn to sell Mark on the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin presses Charles to specify what equity he is offering for the million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles proposes Mark takes three hundred thousand and the rest split seven hundred thousand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark revises his offer to five hundred thousand dollars for fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert summarizes the proposed syndicate deal: one million dollars total for thirty percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles thinks for a moment and then enthusiastically says to do it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that there is a reason the champagne is already open.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles asks the sharks for a second to make a phone call to his CFO.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark agrees to let Charles make the phone call.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles calls his CFO to discuss the million dollar offer from all five sharks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: While Charles is away, Kevin asks the other sharks who wants to bet on the outcome.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond responds to Kevin, betting twenty-five.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert welcomes Charles back and reiterates the terms of the million dollar syndicate offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Charles accepts the million dollar offer for thirty percent from all five sharks.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark proposes they all have a toast to celebrate the deal.

decisions.note: Mark offers 500k for 20% to secure the deal early.
Kevin offers his standard deal, pointing out it is less dilutive.
Robert joins Kevin's offer, adding another 250k.
Lori joins Kevin and Robert, making the combined offer 750k for 30%.
Daymond offers the original ask independently.

decisions.terms: Joins syndicate if Mark is in
decisions.note: Daymond agrees to join an all-shark syndicate if Mark participates.
Mark agrees to the syndicate deal, taking half the equity and putting up half the money.
Charles accepts the combined offer from all five sharks.

record.notes: The pitch includes a demonstration involving handing out champagne, which is coded as 'demonstrates'. The negotiation is complex, involving all five sharks forming a single syndicate.
